about.title: Huron Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Huron is a small place—about 6,836 residents in the farmland of western Fresno County—and when someone dies here, the loss is felt on nearly every block. A wrongful death claim is the civil path a family can take when a death was caused by another party's carelessness, whether by a driver, a property owner, an employer's contractor, or a manufacturer. It moves on its own track, entirely separate from anything the district attorney may or may not pursue. Public collision records for Huron list Lassen Avenue, Palmer Avenue, S Lassen Avenue, and 4th Street as the corridors with the highest counts, and the final 2025 tally shows zero traffic deaths inside the city. That is welcome news, but fatal harm is not limited to city streets or to a single year; farm equipment, work sites, and highway travel to and from Huron all carry real risk. LawProactive does not practice law. We listen, and then we connect you—free of charge—with an independent attorney who takes wrongful death cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Huron Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits standing in a wrongful death case: a surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first, followed by certain dependents and heirs. An attorney can sort out where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Attention to the two-year clock
items.desc: Most wrongful death actions must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is considerably shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Early contact keeps those options open.

items.title: A full accounting of what was lost
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial expenses to include the financial support your loved one would have provided and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so pursuing these losses does not require money up front.

items.question: My brother died in a crash on the road between Huron and the highway. Can I file a wrongful death claim?
items.answer: It depends on who else survives him. California gives priority to a spouse or domestic partner and children; siblings and other relatives generally have standing only if they were financially dependent on him or qualify as heirs when no closer relatives exist. An attorney can review your family's situation and explain whether you are eligible to bring the claim or join one.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges in Fresno County. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil matter and proceeds independently of any criminal prosecution. The two cases have different goals and different standards of proof, so a family can pursue compensation whether or not charges are filed or result in a conviction. Waiting can be risky, because the two-year civil deadline keeps running regardless of what happens in criminal court.

items.question: What if the death involved a county vehicle or a poorly maintained public road near Lassen Avenue?
items.answer: Claims against a government entity in California follow a different and much shorter process than a claim against a private party. A formal claim usually must be presented to the agency within six months of the death before any lawsuit can be filed. Because that window closes quickly, it helps to speak with an attorney as soon as you are able.
